title: Agents Building Agents - Alfonso Graziano, Nearform
talk_summary: Nearform describes an eval-driven optimization loop where a coding agent (Claude Code) iteratively edits a target agent's prompt/tools, runs a golden-dataset eval suite, and keeps or rolls back each hypothesis on a branch. They also mine live user feedback/traces, cluster failure modes, and convert them into new eval cases and fixes. The core transferable idea is a golden dataset + scorer + branch-per-hypothesis optimization loop with human guardrails against gaming the evals.

takeaways.technique: Golden dataset + scorer as regression suite for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain a golden dataset (inputs + expected outputs, including expected tool calls/chains) and scorers that produce an accuracy number, so they have a baseline and can detect regressions over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can see the golden dataset as a test suite, but in a non-deterministic scenario.
takeaways.numbers: Baseline 18% -> 83% in ~10 iterations on naive agent; 67% -> 86% on a real production agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Each iteration: new branch, form one hypothesis, edit agent, run evals, write report.md, update a global memory file; keep branch if metrics improve, roll back if regression.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every iteration starts with a new branch. We create an hypothesis... if the metrics improved, then we continue from this branch.
takeaways.numbers: +10% on already human-optimized production agent evals

takeaways.technique: Human guardrail: forbid editing evals/scorers to pass
takeaways.what_they_do: Human-in-the-loop explicitly instructs the coding agent it may not modify the golden dataset or scorers just to make evals pass, preventing reward hacking.
takeaways.evidence_quote: updating the golden data sets or the scorers just to let the evals pass is not a good idea, so we want to enforce... to not do that

takeaways.technique: Live-feedback trace mining -> failure clusters -> new eval cases
takeaways.what_they_do: Collect user thumbs/annotated traces, run a skill that clusters failure modes and does root-cause analysis against the code, produce a markdown report, triage with SMEs, then fix and add each failure mode to the golden dataset.
takeaways.numbers: 114 traces analyzed; report cadence ~once per sprint

takeaways.technique: Baseline report + memory file as agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: Before optimizing, run evals once to generate a baseline report (what works/fails, per-case detail) plus a persistent global memory file; the coding agent reads both to form hypotheses.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it contains what are the cases, it contains summary, what's working, what's not working... a global memory file across all the runs

takeaways.what_they_do: After clustering/root-cause analysis, run an adversarial review pass over the clusters before proposing fixes, to filter false positives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: then we do an adversarial review of that... we do also a little bit of root cause analysis
